# Tsumly — full site text

> built by Nadeem Mazhar (Nadeem Dev Apps), a solo developer in Pakistan.

## Overview

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/my-web/products/tsumly/

### Every amount adds up.

Tsumly is a **local-first** personal expense and loan ledger for Android:
your money stays on your device — **no account, no cloud by default** —
with an optional encrypted Google Drive backup. It tracks **income,
expenses and transfers** between accounts, and its **smart multi-loan
repayment split** spreads one repayment across several loans, while
**pre-app loans** record older loans without moving your balance.

Free. Android. No account needed.

### Why Tsumly?

The name is inspired by the Japanese verb **tsumu** (積む) — to stack, to
accumulate, to build up over time.

- **Stack** — Tsumu means to stack. Every amount stacks onto the last — a
  loan, a repayment, a rupee at a time — until the ledger is complete.
- **Accumulate** — Small amounts, recorded honestly, **accumulate into the
  full picture**: what you are owed, and what you owe.
- **Build up** — Over weeks and months the ledger **builds up into a record
  you can trust** — and a history you can share.

### How it works — A ledger that lives on your phone.

Tsumly is a **local-first ledger** for the money you **lend and borrow**.
Record a loan, note who it is with, and keep a **running balance** —
everything is stored on your device, and it works offline.

- **Lend or borrow** — record a loan in either direction, with its due
  amount, fees, and history.
- **Partial repayments** — a loan can be paid back a little at a time, and
  every payment is recorded against the same loan.
- **Running balance** — always see where you stand: what you are owed, and
  what you owe.
- **Settle in full** — pay off a loan's full remaining balance in one step,
  after a confirmation.
- **Edits stay honest** — a loan's note and due date can be edited, and a
  loan with no repayments can be deleted; the money itself only moves
  through repayments.

### Smart repayment split — One repayment, split across every loan it covers.

When someone pays you back, the money rarely matches a single loan. Tsumly
**splits one repayment across several active loans** in a single action —
and **never merges loans**, so each loan keeps its own history.

- **Pre-selected for you** — Tsumly picks the loans the repayment applies
  to, and shows which will be **fully paid** and which **partially**.
- **No merging** — a Rs. 3,000 loan repaid by Rs. 1,170 stays one loan with
  **Rs. 1,830 left**.
- **Mistakes are reversible** — a repayment recorded by mistake can be
  **reversed in one step**.
- **Smallest first** — the split pays the smallest outstanding loan first,
  and the oldest loan first when two are equal.
- **Overpayment is blocked** — a repayment cannot be more than the selected
  loans' total outstanding.
- **Auto-select, on by default** — Tsumly pre-selects all of a person's
  open loans; turn it off in settings to pick by hand.
- **Every split is recorded** — each repayment stores how much landed on
  each loan, and the balance before and after, so statements can show the
  breakdown.

### Pre-app loans — Loans from before the app still count.

You were lending and borrowing long before Tsumly. **Pre-app loans**
record those older loans **without moving your current balance** — so your
history is complete and your balance stays honest.

- **Mark it pre-app** — when you create a loan that started before the app,
  it is recorded without an opening balance movement.
- **Same detail, same history** — every loan keeps its own due amount,
  fees, and history, pre-app or not.
- **Flip it later** — marking a loan pre-app adds its opening movement
  back to the account; removing the mark records it. The amount, due date
  and repayments stay unchanged.

### Person profiles — People, not just numbers.

Loans live on **person profiles**, so you always see **who owes what**.
Each person carries their own totals, and nothing about an open loan can
be hidden by accident.

- **Per-person totals** — every profile shows what that person owes you,
  and what you owe them.
- **Archive is guarded** — a person with **outstanding loans cannot be
  archived**.
- **Archived people stay reachable** — they still appear in the person
  picker, and picking one **restores them automatically**.
- **Delete is refused while loans exist** — a person with any loan cannot
  be deleted; archive them instead.
- **A full ledger per person** — loans opened and repayments made in one
  interleaved history, with open and paid loan counts.

### Everyday money — Income, expenses and transfers — in the same ledger.

Tsumly tracks the everyday money too — **income and expenses** against
categories and accounts, and **transfers between your own accounts** — so
the loan ledger and the cash ledger always agree.

- **Income & expenses** — record money in and money out against an account
  and a category, with an optional note, fee and tax on every entry.
- **Transfers between accounts** — move money from one account to another
  in one entry, with its own fee and tax; deleting a transfer removes both
  legs and puts the balances back.
- **Fees & taxes, kept visible** — every income, expense, transfer, loan
  and repayment can carry a fee and a tax, and monthly reports total them
  separately.
- **Categories with subcategories** — starter categories for Pakistani
  households, including Salary, Business, Freelance, Groceries and
  Transport, with subcategories such as Supermarket and Local Market; add,
  rename or archive your own, two levels deep.
- **Dates you control** — entries carry the date and time you choose, and
  an entry keeps the clock time you recorded even when you travel across
  timezones.

### Accounts — Every rupee lives in an account.

Cash, a bank, JazzCash, Easypaisa or another wallet — each account has its
own **opening balance** and a live balance that follows every movement.

- **Opening balance per account** — start each account with the money
  already in it; its balance is the opening balance plus every movement
  since.
- **Five account types** — Cash, Bank, JazzCash, Easypaisa and Other, each
  with its own icon.
- **Archive, never delete** — archiving an account keeps its history
  intact, and archived accounts are excluded from your available balance.
- **Balance guard** — when a payment would take an account below zero,
  Tsumly either warns you and waits for confirmation, or blocks it — your
  choice in settings.

### Reports & statements — Where the money went, on one screen — and on paper.

Monthly reports show **where the money went**, and statements turn any
slice of the ledger into a **PDF you can share**.

- **Monthly reports** — cash in, cash out and net for any month, with
  income and expense broken down by category, a weekly cash-flow chart,
  fees and taxes totalled, and lent and borrowed positions.
- **Six statement exports** — all activity, expense, income, loans,
  transfers and per-account statements, each as a PDF.
- **Per-person statements** — from any person's profile, export their
  loans and repayments as a PDF for a date range you pick: last 30 or 90
  days, last 6 months, last year, all time, or a custom range.
- **Repayment breakdowns on statements** — every repayment shows how it
  was split across loans, because each split is stored with the repayment.
- **Share or save** — every statement PDF can be shared from the system
  share sheet or saved as a file.

### Home dashboard — Your money, the moment you open the app.

The home tab opens on your **available balance**, your **net position**,
and what you have **lent and borrowed** — with one-tap actions for income,
expense, transfer or a loan payment.

- **Available balance & net position** — the balance across your active
  accounts, with the net position underneath it; either can be hidden in
  settings.
- **Lent & borrowed at a glance** — two tiles show what others owe you and
  what you owe, always live.
- **Quick actions** — Income, Expense, Transfer and Loan from one row; the
  Loan action opens the smart repayment flow for a person.
- **Daily quote** — a short quote under the greeting, drawn from a bundled
  set, with Urdu quotes shown right-to-left in a Nastaliq or Naskh font
  you pick.
- **Pull to refresh** — a pull refreshes every number on the dashboard.

### Loan reminders — A due date that reminds you itself.

A loan with a due date reminds you on its own: a local notification on
the **due date at 9:00 AM**, and an **overdue reminder the next morning**
if it is still open.

- **Due-date reminders** — set an optional due date when you create a loan;
  Tsumly schedules a 9:00 AM reminder for the day and an overdue reminder
  the next day.
- **Tapping opens the loan** — a reminder opens the loan's detail screen,
  ready to record the repayment.
- **Reminders follow the loan** — editing a due date reschedules its
  reminders, and deleting a loan cancels them.

### Make it yours — Light or dark, your font, your currency.

Tsumly bends to how you like it: **light or dark**, your **display font**,
and which numbers the home tab shows.

- **Theme & display font** — System, Dark or Light theme, and Bricolage
  Grotesque or EB Garamond for headings.
- **Show or hide** — available balance, net position and animated amounts
  can each be switched off.
- **One base currency** — pick from 15 currencies on first run, PKR
  pre-selected; everything is recorded in that one currency.
- **Your name on the greeting** — the home greeting uses the display name
  you set in settings.
- **Date & time control** — allow changing the date and time on entries, or
  lock them to now.

### Backup & privacy — Your money stays yours.

**Offline-first and one-device-first.** Nothing leaves the phone unless
you turn on Drive backup — and even then, the backup is **encrypted** and
stored in the app's **own private Drive folder**.

- **No account, no cloud by default** — your money stays on your device;
  there is nothing to sign up for.
- **Encrypted backup** — the optional Google Drive backup is encrypted
  with **AES-256-GCM**.
- **No tracking** — no analytics, no ads, nothing phoning home.
- **Sign-in stays on the device** — device-specific sign-in details never
  leave the phone in a portable backup.
- **Local backup file** — export everything to a timestamped
  **.moneybackup** file and restore it on any device; older backups are
  migrated on import.
- **Scheduled Drive backups** — hourly, daily, weekly or monthly automatic
  uploads to your private Drive folder, keeping the latest three.
- **Password protection** — an optional password of at least 8 characters
  encrypts a backup (AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2 with 600,000 iterations);
  scheduled uploads can reuse a password kept in the Android Keystore.
- **Restore on first run** — a fresh install offers to restore from a
  local backup file or from Drive before you set anything up.

### FAQ — Questions, answered.

**Is my money data stored on a server?**

No. Tsumly is local-first: your accounts, transactions, loans and settings
live in a local database on your device. There is no Tsumly account and no
sign-up, no analytics, no ads, and nothing phoning home. The only thing
that ever leaves the phone is a backup you choose to make — an encrypted
Google Drive backup to your own private Drive folder, or a .moneybackup
file you export yourself.

**Can I record loans from before I started using the app?**

Yes — pre-app loans record older loans without moving your current
balance, so your history is complete and your balance stays honest. You
can flip a loan’s pre-app mark later; the amount, due date and repayments
stay unchanged.

**What if someone pays back more than the loans add up to?**

That cannot happen by mistake: a repayment cannot be more than the
selected loans’ total outstanding. The split pays the smallest outstanding
loan first, and the oldest first when two are equal — and a repayment
recorded by mistake can be reversed in one step.

**Does Tsumly work offline?**

Yes. Everything is stored on your device and the app works offline. The
only features that need the internet are the optional Google Drive backup
and restore.

**Can I export my records?**

Yes. Monthly reports show cash in, cash out and net by category, and
statements turn any slice of the ledger into a PDF you can share: all
activity, expense, income, loans, transfers and per-account statements,
plus per-person statements for any date range you pick. You can also
export everything to a timestamped .moneybackup file and restore it on
any device.

**What does Tsumly cost?**

Nothing. Tsumly is free — no account, no subscription, no ads. Your money
stays on your device.

## Privacy Policy

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/my-web/products/tsumly/privacy/

Tsumly collects no personal data. Everything stays on your device unless
you choose to back it up.

### The short version

Tsumly is private by design. It does not collect, track, profile, or
upload personal data. No Tsumly account or signup is required, and there
are no analytics, advertising, or tracking SDKs. Your records stay on this
device unless you choose to make a backup. If you choose Google Drive
backup, Google Sign-In and Google Drive process the account and
authentication information needed to provide that feature.

### What stays on your device

Your accounts, transactions, transfers, loans, repayments, people,
categories, settings, and optional profile name are stored only in the
app's local database (SQLite) on your phone. Uninstalling the app (or
clearing its data) removes them. Android automatic backup is disabled for
the app, so the operating system never silently copies your data to the
cloud.

### Local backups

Exporting a backup produces a file you control (.moneybackup), and import
is validated before anything is written. An unencrypted backup file
contains readable financial data — store it privately, like you would any
sensitive document.

### Google Drive backup (optional)

Drive backup is optional and off by default. If you sign in, Tsumly
uploads backup files to the hidden appDataFolder of your own Google
account. The app requests only the drive.appdata OAuth scope
(https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.appdata), which limits it to its
own hidden folder — it cannot see, list, or access any other files in your
Drive. Backups never pass through any server run by us (we run none). You
can disconnect your Google account at any time in Settings; disconnecting
stops future uploads but does not delete backups already on your Drive. To
remember the connected account, the app stores your Google account’s email
and display name locally on the device. This identity is never uploaded
anywhere except inside backups you create yourself — and it is excluded
from portable backup files, so restoring a backup on another device never
shows a stale "connected" state. Your Google authentication tokens are
managed by Google Sign-In on the device and are never written into backup
files.

### Scheduled backups

You can optionally enable automatic backups (hourly, daily, weekly, or
monthly). Scheduled backups use the same export and upload as manual ones:
the app checks first whether your data has actually changed, and skips the
upload when there is nothing new to back up.

### Optional password encryption

You can protect a backup with a password. The backup is encrypted with
AES-256-GCM using a key derived from your password via PBKDF2. The
password is kept only in this device’s secure storage (Android Keystore)
— it never leaves the device and is never included in the backup itself.
There is no way to recover a forgotten password: an encrypted backup whose
password is lost cannot be restored.

### Your choices

Your data is yours. You can export it, delete backup files, disconnect
Google Drive, or uninstall the app at any time to remove its local data
from the device.

### Changes to this policy

This policy may be updated from time to time; the version on this page is
always the current one. If the app ever starts handling data in a new way,
the policy will say so.

### Contact

Questions about privacy? Email nadeem.devapps@gmail.com.

## Terms of Use

https://nadeemdevapps.github.io/my-web/products/tsumly/terms/

Tsumly is a personal finance tracker, provided as-is. Your data stays on
your device by default.

### Acceptance

By installing and using Tsumly, you agree to these terms. If you do not
agree with any part of them, please do not use the app.

### What Tsumly does

Tsumly is a record-keeping tool for tracking your own accounts, income,
expenses, transfers, loans, and repayments. It is meant for lawful personal
finance tracking. Tsumly is not financial advice, and it is not a bank or
payment service — please double-check important numbers yourself before
acting on them.

### Local-first, no Tsumly account

Tsumly stores everything in a local database (SQLite) on your device.
There is no Tsumly account and no sign-up, and Tsumly operates no server
that receives your financial records. On Android the app opts out of
automatic cloud backup (allowBackup=false), so a fresh install starts
empty and uninstalling the app wipes its local data. If you choose Google
Drive backup, backup files are uploaded directly to your own Google
account — see the Privacy Policy for details.

### Your data is yours

You own everything you record in Tsumly. By default your data lives only
on your device, you are responsible for keeping your own backups.
Uninstalling the app, clearing its data, or losing the device can
permanently remove your records — export a backup before changing devices
or uninstalling.

### Acceptable use

Use Tsumly for lawful personal finance tracking only. You may not use the
app to record, conceal, or facilitate anything illegal.

### Provided as-is

Tsumly is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties of any
kind, express or implied, including any implied warranty of fitness for a
particular purpose. To the extent permitted by law, the developer is not
liable for any loss or damage arising from your use of the app.

### Stopping use

You can stop using Tsumly at any time. Uninstalling the app deletes its
local data from the device. Any backup files you created — including
backups on your own Google Drive — stay where you put them until you delete
them yourself.

### Changes to these terms

These terms may be updated from time to time. The version on this page is
always the current one.

### Contact

Questions about these terms? Email nadeem.devapps@gmail.com.
